name: Heliotrope Grey
lede: Heliotrope Grey is a pale, greyed purple named for the heliotrope flower, present in a small slice of our painting archive since the 1400s.

sections.title: A greyed heliotrope
sections.body:
The library files Heliotrope Grey from the 1912 Ridgway atlas, plate L, hue 65, tone d; the ISCC-NBS system placed it in block 227 in 1955, and Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary also carries it, at plate 44 C3 [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[deep-vinaceous-lavender]], [[catalpa]], [[deep-greyish-lavender]] and [[dark-lavender]], at 3, 3.5, 
In LCH terms it measures lightness 65, chroma 12, hue 327 degrees, the ISCC-NBS "pale purple" block, Munsell 7.8P 6.4/3.1, a step between [[purple]] and [[violet]] [1]. 5, 4.7 and 5.4 ΔE [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds this color in 48 of 23,781 paintings, 0.2 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 24 [2]. That makes it rarer than 59 percent of the named colors we track [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 8 of 1,674 paintings, at 0.5 percent of that century's paintings, 3.1 times the expected rate [2]. Inside a painting it most often sits as a mid-tone, in 38 percent of its appearances, by lightness rank rather than by eye [2].

The earliest match in our archive is dated 1474, by Piero della Francesca; the name's own first record comes 438 years later, in 1912, so the match is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not evidence the pigment itself is that old, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].
